title: Stock Market Today Live, October 22: Sensex falls 458 points, Nifty drops 170; over 400 stocks hit 52-week lows - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 22nd October 2026.

At 2.20 p.m. on October 22, the Sensex was down 458.05 points, or 0.62 per cent, at 73,251.64, while the Nifty fell 169.65 points, or 0.74 per cent, to 22,641.70.

Of the 3,598 stocks traded on the NSE, 952 advanced, 2,548 declined and 98 remained unchanged.

A total of 21 stocks touched their 52-week highs, 403 hit 52-week lows, 51 stocks reached the upper circuit and 176 hit the lower circuit.

Five stocks on the Nifty 50 managed to post gains by afternoon. Bajaj Finance was the top performer, rising 1.47 per cent to ₹939.60 from a previous close of ₹926.00, followed by Bajaj Auto, which gained 1.26 per cent to ₹10,199 from ₹10,072. Larsen & Toubro rose 1.16 per cent to ₹3,678.10 from ₹3,636, Bharti Airtel advanced 1.05 per cent to ₹1,911.50 from ₹1,891.70, and UltraTech Cement added 0.98 per cent to ₹10,955 from ₹10,849.

On the losing side, Nestle India was the biggest laggard, down 2.19 per cent to ₹1,197.10 from ₹1,223.90. Tech Mahindra fell 1.86 per cent to ₹1,800.60 from ₹1,834.70, HDFC Bank declined 1.85 per cent to ₹693.85 from ₹706.95, Coal India shed 1.78 per cent to ₹400.25 from ₹407.50, and HDFC Life slipped 1.65 per cent to ₹530.75 from ₹539.65. Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank and Infosys were the top three negative contributors to the Nifty by index weight.

* Trend: Bearish, with Nifty 50 down 0.61 per cent at 22,670 and market breadth negative at 6 advances against 44 declines.

* Immediate support: 22,530–22,500. A decisive break below 22,500 could drag the index down to 22,420–22,400.

* Immediate resistance: 22,810–22,830. A decisive break above 22,830 could ease downside pressure and lift the index to 22,950–23,000.

* Futures resistance: 22,790. A decisive break above this level could take October futures to 22,920; failure to breach it could trigger a decline towards 22,500.

* Trading strategy: Consider long positions in October futures only on a break above 22,790, with a stop-loss at 22,760 and a target of 22,880, following the prescribed trailing stop-loss strategy.

According to Vallum Capital Advisors’ monthly report, Indian equity categories declined during the month, with India Equity funds falling 1.5%. However, net fund inflows into India Equity increased to ₹39,071 crore from ₹31,424 crore in August, reflecting continued investor participation despite market volatility. In contrast, dynamic strategies saw net outflows of ₹2,904 crore, compared with inflows of ₹11,276 crore in the previous month.

Vallum Capital notes that higher rates hit metals, AI doubts reshuffled global tech, and a firmer rupee cushioned the damage at home. Indian investors kept buying through it all. The question now is whether this is a pause before old leaders return or the start of a new order led by the businesses that put AI to work, with Quality as the new market compass.

Mr. Mukesh Choudhary, Managing Director, Accuspace, a real estate company

Jaipur has an immense potential to attract large corporate occupiers and support sizeable Grade A developments. It reinforces the fact that demand in the city is moving beyond conventional retail and commercial spaces towards organised developments. Favourable policy support, talent pool, and infrastructure growth are reshaping the city’s commercial real estate landscape.

Occupiers are no longer choosing Jaipur only for its cost efficiencies. They are scaling here because it offers an exceptional talent pool, robust connectivity infrastructure, and a modern lifestyle that retains top professionals.

There is an aggressive expansion happening in Southern Jaipur in areas like Tonk Road, Sitapura, and along the Ajmer Road. The market is seeing an influx of Grade-A office complexes, modern co-working hubs, and specialized IT/ITeS corporate offices designed to absorb the massive professional workforce.

The commercial real estate portfolio of Jaipur-headquartered real estate company Accuspace has crossed 0.5 million sq. ft. across office, retail and warehousing.

Among the major occupiers in the company’s commercial portfolio includes global technology and consulting firm Accenture which leased 1.23 lakh sq. ft. of office space at ‘The Edge 2’ in Sitapura, organised retailer Zudio which has leased 13,000 sq. ft. at The Edge 1 on Tonk Road and top electrical equipment and home appliances company Havells India which leased 1.2 lakh sq. ft. of warehousing space on Ajmer Road.

The company is also planning a huge mixed-use project in Jaipur that will change face of commercial real estate in the city.

Accuspace specializes in acquiring and developing properties into state-of-the-art warehouses, built-to-suit (BTS) spaces, and plush office spaces. It is leading provider of world-class commercial real estate, delivering trusted, tailored solutions. The company plans to develop over 20 million sq. ft. of commercial space by 2030.
